about: What may differ between BN5's battle (the reference) and BN6's with a family moved in (the subject), and why: tools/xdiff.py reads each game's numbers as BN6's (maps), each game's structures through their own layouts (layouts), and replays BN6's draws from BN5's by the twins of its rng, the engine's own draws one game alone makes named there too (rng), and lets a difference pass only where a mask names it (masks), each an engine difference that is not the family's code, with the evidence: both games' routines by address. No mask applies to the family's own records (its objects, what they own, its attacks and effects): what the engine writes there in its own numbers is read as BN6's in the snapshot, as an enemy id is (maps: alliance, renderer, slot), and any other difference there fails the spec (docs/MULTIROM.md, Transplanted families; docs/DEVTOOLS.md, The differential). No game code here: addresses and numbers only.

name_id.why: An object's NameID (+0x28) is its enemy id: BN5's CanGard family is 0x4F-0x54, moved as BN6's ids 0x200-0x205, and its Handi family 0x13-0x18 as 0x206-0x20B, the families' (src/emu/xvirus_families.c, .first_id; xvirus_recipe.h, XV_FIRST_ID); MegaMan is 0x180 in BN5 and 0x1A0 in BN6 (his battle object's NameID in both traces from their first frame).

megaman_forms.why: MegaMan's NameID in a form of BN6's is 0x1AB + the form (0x08015B22 writes it as he crosses: 0x1AC-0x1C3; 0x1A0 in none), where BN5's stays 0x180 through a Soul and its end (the research's runs/nid). His role is MegaMan's whatever his form; his NameID is compared as BN6 writes it for the form BN5's maps to (a Soul behind the proxy, 0x1B3).

ai_index.why: AIData +1, the AI index the engine finds a family's tables by: CanGard's 14 in BN5, 32 in BN6's grown tables; Handi's 4, 33 (xvirus_cangard and xvirus_handi .src_ai, .ai).

t3_type.why: An attack's type (+1), by its number in BN5 where BN5's is moved: BN6 spawns a moved type of the family's (CanGard's reticle, BN5's third kind's type 0x25) as the second-level dispatch's type of its kind (the first's 0x5C, the third's 0xD2, the fourth's 0x91: xvirus_recipe.h, XV_T*_DISPATCH), its BN5 number in the kind's side table by the object's slot (BN6_DISPATCH_SIDE: the first kind's at 0x0203FF00, the third's at 0x0203FF20, the fourth's at 0x0203FF40), and the dispatch runs it as that number. The trace writes the side table's byte beside each object of a dispatch type (src/dev/xdiff.c, version 3) and the snapshot reads its type as that byte (tools/xdiff_snap.py): a translation, not a mask, so a moved type keeps its BN5 number in both and is the same. The spawn hook reads the dispatch's spawner's frame the same way (its BN5 type and its caller, src/dev/xdiff_events.c). A twin of BN6's is spawned as BN6's own number, and mapped here where the numbers differ (none so far).
evidence: the dispatch's spawner (src/emu/xvirus_dispatch.c, the project's own Thumb): push {r0,lr}; TWIN by the type's low byte; XV_TYPE_MOVED spawns the kind's dispatch type; after BN6's spawner, the type into the side table at the object's slot (+3); its frame above BN6's spawner's five words: the type at +0x1C, its caller at +0x20
the dispatch type's routine: ldrb r0,[r5,#3]; the side table's byte; MOVED's routine for it, r1 the type times four as BN5's runner leaves it (BN5 0x08003014-0x0800301E / BN6 0x080031F4-0x080031FE)
BN6's runner reads +1 alone and its spawn writes it alone (BN6 0x080031F4, 0x080032BE); the moved code never reads it (the installer refuses ldrb rX,[r5,#1] in a moved block)

effect.why: An effect object's id (+4 of the fourth kind's type 0): CanGard's muzzle blast is BN5's 0x57, copied as BN6's 0x6C (the immediate at BN5 0x08108FB6). The Souls' (the Souls track's S4, tools/xsoul.py): ColonelSoul's ScreenDivide's three, BN5's 0x48-0x4A (its family 0x43's base 0x48 + its sub-family, BN5 0x080EEE18), copied as BN6's 0xC0-0xC2 (the Souls' effects 0xC0-0xCF of the grown table, upward, issue #82's shared allocations); ShadowSoul's slash 0x17 (its sword family's sub-family 2, BN5's table 0x080EC112) as 0xC3 and TomahawkSoul's swing 0x45 (BN5 0x080EEFDC) as 0xC4, each with BN5's sprite copied: BN6 has an effect of the same record (0x17, and 0x33 for 0x45: its list, number, animation and palette) whose sprite, redrawn, animates for other frames, and an effect lives as long as its animation.

panel_type.why: A panel's type (+2), the type it is drawn as (+6, the one-frame override's at +8) and the low nibble of its flags (BN5's +0x18, BN6's +0x14, the type ORed into its table's word): BN5's lava (8) and sea (0xA) are BN6's free types 13 and 14 where src/emu/xpanels.c brings them in, BN5's holy (9) BN6's 5 (src/emu/xfields.c), the rest the same numbers.
evidence: the flags: _object_updatePanelParameters ORs the type into its word, BN5 0x0800AFE0 / BN6 IWRAM 0x030078DC (ldrb r1,[r0,#2]; ... orrs r1,r3)

the drawn type: the same routines copy +2 to +6; BN5's per-panel update writes lava's 8 or 2 there as it blinks (0x0800AA68), BN6's its conveyors' own type or 2 (0x0800C478), the path lava and sea take in BN6 (xpanels.c, panel_ages)
the flags' words: lava's 0x11010 and the sea's 0x30010 are BN5's (BN5_PANEL_FLAGS_OF), copied into BN6's grown table (xpanels.c, flags_make)

alliance.why: A collision data's +0x30 (what it is) and +0x34 (what it strikes) are words the engine's setup takes from a table by the object's alliance and a region its caller names, two words a region, and ORs the time stop's bit 0x10000 into +0x30 while time is stopped; each game has its own table (layouts, collision, alliance_masks), whose entries mostly differ by BN6's bit 0x80. So a BN5 word is read as the BN6 entry at its place in BN5's table (with the time stop's bit as it is): over the 160 entries each BN5 word gives one BN6 word (a word two entries would give otherwise would be left as it is; none does). A hit and a touch OR the other object's +0x30 into what hit or touched it (BN6's +0x70 and +0x6C, BN5's +0x68 and +0x64): such a word is read as the OR of the BN6 words of the table's words it is made of, where every way of making it gives the same (else it is compared as it is). Not the family's code: the setup and the hit pass are the engine's, and the family's region and alliance are compared through them (a family object set up with another region reads as another BN6 word).
evidence: the setup: BN5 0x08016760-0x080167AE / BN6 0x08019FB4-0x0801A00C, the same steps: +0x30 from the table's reader (BN5 0x08016BBC / BN6 0x0801A0BA: alliance x 4 + region x 8) for the region in r1, stored at BN5 0x0801678A / BN6 0x08019FE8; 0x10000 ORed in where the time stop's test (BN5 0x08008A78 / BN6 0x0800A098, bit 2 of the battle's flags) is set (BN5 0x08016792-0x0801679C / BN6 0x08019FF0-0x08019FFA); +0x34 for the region in r2 (BN5 0x080167A6 / BN6 0x0801A004)

the tables (layouts, collision, alliance_masks): BN5 0x08016364 reads 0x08410000, 0x04210000, 0x80000000, 0x40000000 (entries 2, 3, 8, 9) where BN6 0x08019C7C reads 0x08410080, 0x04210080, 0x80000080, 0x40000080; entries 4-7, 10, 11 alike in both; of BN5's 160 words 128 have their BN6 entry with the bit, 30 the same word, region 61's two (BN5 0x80000080, 0x40000080) BN6's 0x80

the hit pass ORs the hitter's +0x30 into what hit it: BN5 0x080169E8-0x080169F2, 0x08016A28-0x08016A34 (its +0x6C/+0x70, then +0x68) / BN6 0x081D7800-0x081D7804, 0x081D783A-0x081D7840 (+0x70); the second pass into what touched it: BN5 0x080174AA-0x080174B0 (+0x64) / BN6 0x081D7BD2-0x081D7BD8 (+0x6C)
BN6's use of its bit: its second pass lets an object whose +0x3C has 0x20 touch only one whose +0x30 has 0x80 (0x081D7BAE-0x081D7BD0); BN5's twin 0x0801748C has no such test

in the traces of every spec each +0x30 and +0x34, and each hit and touch word on the frames compared, reads as its BN6 word: MegaMan's 0x08410000, CanGard's and the Mettaur's 0x04210000, the reticle's 0x40000000, MegaMan's shots' 0x80000000, each with 0x80 in BN6; a reticle's hit word 0x08410000 (MegaMan's) as 0x08410080

renderer.why: Each frame the sprite renderer hands each object it draws a place for its tiles in OBJ VRAM (its sprite state's +0x08, u16) from a running count over all it draws before it, and a palette slot (+0x15's high nibble) from the slots taken before it; a frame or palette already loaded this frame is given its place or slot again. The code is the same in both games, but what each draws (MegaMan's own sprite, his flash and sparks, BN6's own effects, a native) differs, so the numbers do. A family object's place and slot are read as their rank among those the family's objects drawn that frame take: the family's own draw order and sharing, compared; what else is drawn among them is no part of the family's. One not drawn (its +0x00 bit 0x02 clear) keeps the place it was last drawn at, so it keeps that rank; one never drawn, or whose place moved undrawn, is compared as it is. Slot 15 (none taken) stays. The frames the family draws are compared from its sprite's own data (+0x1C, +0x20) and its cache (+0x24), so its tile counts are. The same places of what is not the family's are masked (the renderer's slots, the renderer's palette slot).
evidence: the renderer: BN5 0x081C7F26-0x081C804C and BN6 0x081D64BE-0x081D65E4 (the IWRAM renderer's ROM copies), the same code but for their literal pools

the tile place: BN5 0x081C7FF4-0x081C7FFC / BN6 0x081D658C-0x081D6594, the running count's value stored and the frame's tiles added to it (BN6 0x081D6562-0x081D6566, 0x081D6590-0x081D6594); a frame already copied this frame is given its place again (found at BN6 0x081D66A8-0x081D66C6, stored at 0x081D65B8); a sprite not drawn keeps its old place, its cache cleared (BN6 0x081D653A-0x081D6544)

the palette slot: BN5 0x081C803A-0x081C8048 / BN6 0x081D65D2-0x081D65E0, the slot's number shifted into +0x15's high nibble, none where it reads 0xF (BN6 0x081D65BE-0x081D65C8); the slot found or taken: BN6 0x081D6640-0x081D666A

in every spec the family's ranks are the same in both games on every frame a family object is drawn in both (cangard_v1: 2084 tile places, 2084 palette slots; cangard_v1_keys: 1813 and 1798), with no family object drawn in one game alone

slot.why: An object's header +3 is its slot in its kind's array, which the engine hands out to the first free one. Objects are matched by role (what they are, in the order they appeared), never by slot, so +3 is read as counted from the object's own slot: 0 where it is its own, as the engine writes it, so a slot taken in one game and not the other (an effect living a frame longer) is no difference of the object's.
evidence: the slot is the first free bit of the kind's bitmap: BN5 0x080030B4-0x080030C2 / BN6 0x08003294-0x080032A2 (the same code); the spawn clears the object from +4 on (BN5 0x080030CC-0x080030D2 / BN6 0x080032AC-0x080032B2) and writes +0 and +1, leaving +3 as the slot holds it
in both traces of cangard_v1_keys every object's +3 equals its slot (5856 objects in BN5's, 5822 in BN6's)

action.why: CurAction (+9). A virus's: BN5 numbers generic states 0-5 and its own from 6, BN6 generic 0-7 and its own from 8 (two status states, frozen and bubbled, between), so BN5's 0-5 are BN6's 0-5, its 6 BN6's 8, 7 on two up (every family table in both ROMs; the attack's end writes 6 at BN5 0x0800F2E2 and 8 at BN6 0x08011754). MegaMan's: ready 6 in BN5, 8 in BN6 (BN5_MEGAMAN_READY, BN6_MEGAMAN_READY), his others the same (a step 0x10, hit 3, seen in both traces). The same numbering holds for an attack of the third kind that runs the same states: its state table BN5's generic 0-5 and its own from 6, BN6's 0-7 and its own from 8 (t3_types; Handi's obstacle, the third kind's type 0x4B, run by BN5 0x08017FCC / BN6 0x0801B394 from its state table BN5 0x080CF118, 8 entries, BN6 0x080CF264, 10: its own 6 and 7 BN6's 8 and 9). MegaMan's actions of a family (CurAction from 0x10, run from each game's table of families, BN5 0x080EB514, Gregar 0x080EBFA0) by the twin of each: BN5's 0x1A, the Soul's unison and its end (the player update 0x08014604 sets it from AIData +0x44's bits 0x4000 and 0x40), is BN6's 0x1C, the Cross's and Beast Out's (its twin 0x08017BC0, the same steps); BN5's 0x1E, the plain charged shot (0x080ECAB8), is BN6's 0x16 (0x080ED140), the same phases but BN5's first: it tests the battle's flag 0x40 (0x080ECAE0) and fires at once where it is clear, where BN6's always waits 5 frames first (0x080ED168), so a charged shot parts the two games (no spec fires one: docs/DEVTOOLS.md, The differential). The step (0x10), the buster (0x11) and the Cannon's (0x14) are the same number in both. A Soul's charged shots run as the families the Souls track moved (S4: BN6's attack families grown, xattack_grow.c, the Souls' from 0xC0 in tools/xsoul.py's FAMILIES' order): BN5's 0x43 (ColonelSoul's) BN6's 0xC0, 0x3A (NumberSoul's) 0xC1, 0x40 (KnightSoul's) 0xC2, 0x50 (ToadSoul's) 0xC3, 0x3D (ShadowSoul's B+Left) 0xC4, 0x45 (TomahawkSoul's) 0xC5, and 0x13 by his attack (megaman_by_attack).

megaman_by_attack.why: BN5's sword family (0x13, 0x080EBDC6) runs ShadowSoul's charged shot as its sub-family 2 (his AttackVars +3, AI data +0xA3, set by its power attack 0x0800F818) and the sword chips as the others; BN6's 0x13 is its own sword family (0x080ECAB6, no twin of BN5's), which BN6's sword chips run, so the Souls' copy of BN5's runs as 0xC6 (xattack_grow.h's Souls' numbers, tools/xsoul.py's FAMILIES): BN5's 0x13 is BN6's 0xC6 where his sub-family is 2, BN6's 0x13 otherwise

sound.why: A sound is compared by its song number: the music player it plays on is its song table entry's, each game's own (song 0x6A, MegaMan's buster's, is BN5's player 22 and BN6's player 0; the reticle's 0xAE player 4 in both). BN5's songs a Soul's code plays that Gregar's table has otherwise (another sound at that number) are copied, the Souls track's S4, into BN6's empty song slots, each sound at the slot issue #82's allocations give it whatever track copies it (their amendment: the first install copies it, the others find it there), each on its own music player (src/audio/xsong.c's xsong_put, from src/emu/soulpower.c; tools/xsoul.py's SONGS): BN5's 0x70 is BN6's slot 0x5F, 0x117 0x5E, 0x115 0x5A, read so where BN6 played that slot (bn5_to_bn6). The differential finds a song by the core's song table (src/dev/xdiff.c), the slots as the install left them.
evidence: the song tables: BN5 0x08155BF4, BN6 0x08159F48 (RomLayout.song_table), 8 bytes a song: its header, its player

family_effects.why: Effects (the fourth kind's type 0) name no object that spawned them; those of the effect ids the family's code spawns are the family's, compared as such: its muzzle's blast (BN5's 0x57, BN6's 0x6C: BN5 0x08108FB6) and its reticle's strike (0x0E: BN5 0x080C9660-0x080C9662). Any other effect is the engine's or another enemy's (in the smoke spec the Mettaur's 0x14), which stops a spec as MegaMan's own state does.

rom_tables.why: A pointer into each game's own ROM is read by the data there (32 bytes the same: a table both games have). Where a table's end is followed by other bytes in each game, the 32 bytes from its last entries run past it: such a table is named here, by its place in both and its entries' size and count, and a pointer into it is read as its place in it, the entry there the same bytes in both (else the entry differs, and so does the pointer).

tables.name: Handi's bomb's kinds
tables.why: the third kind's type 0x4B (the obstacle Handi drops) keeps at +0x60 the entry of its kind (its +4) in this table: its sprite's animation, HP and collision's region and alliance; Handi's kinds are 2-7 (its version's pair, BN5 0x08106330-0x08106336)
evidence: the obstacle's spawner BN5 0x080CF37E / BN6 0x080CF4EC: +0x60 = the table + 8 x +4 (BN5 0x080CF396-0x080CF3A0, the table's one literal 0x080CF43C / BN6 0x080CF504-0x080CF50E, 0x080CF5B0)
the tables' 64 bytes the same in both but entry 1's HP (BN5 300, BN6 200, +2): the bytes after them are each game's own code and pools

form.why: MegaMan's form, his battle NaviStats' +0x2C and his pending form's +0 (the player block, src/dev/xdiff.c): BN5 numbers a Soul by its Navi's AI index (7-12 Team Colonel's), BN6 a Cross 1-10, Beast Out 0xB-0x18. BN5's Souls stand behind BN6's form 8, the proxy (src/emu/soulproxy.c, the Souls track's S1), and which Soul it is lives in the Souls' block (BN6_SOULS, its +0: compared with BN5's form byte through maps, souls); 0 (none) and 0xFF (none pending) are the same in both.
evidence: BN5: the form byte written as he unites (0x08010DDA from 0x08012106), the Soul's AI index (KnightSoul 11 in soul_knight's trace from t1)

BN6: OK's commit of UNITE writes the record's form 8 (src/emu/soulunite.c, the hook at 0x08029150), which the turn's crossing writes into his NaviStats (0x08014C5C); the Soul into BN6_SOULS as the proxy's overlay entry runs (src/emu/soullife.c)

sprites.why: A sprite is compared by what it is, not by where each game keeps it: a sprite state's data pointer (+0x18, the sprite's start + 4) named by the registry's pair, the same list and entry of each game's sprite lists (BN6's RomLayout.sprite_lists 0x08031CC4, BN5's XRomLayout's 0x0803272C: a word per list, a word per entry). Where either game's pointer is one of a pair's, both must be that pair's: MegaMan drawn from another sprite, his flash or a spark another, is a difference. A sprite of no pair (a moved family's, BN5's from its battle's cache in EWRAM) is compared as before, its frames from its own data.

copies.why: A sprite of BN5's that the install copies into BN6's ROM copy by its bytes (a recipe's sprites BN6 has none of the same bytes of: the Souls', tools/xsoul.py) is that sprite: BN6's pointer at the copy is named as BN5's entry where the registry names it (MegaMan's buster's first flash in a Soul: BN5's list 3 entry 3, its bytes copied to list 0's 0x4C, where BN6's own entry 3 is a redrawn one).
evidence: soulcode_bn5.c's sprites (BN5's list and number, BN6's, the copy's place in the Souls' room: soul_room.h's SOULS_ART, free_space.h's FREE_SOULS), each copied whole from BN5's ROM by src/emu/soulcode.c's art_move; soul_buster: BN5's 'his buster's first flash' and BN6's copy at 0x08C87400
MegaMan's object's sprite state in both traces from t1: BN5 0x081C9804, BN6 0x081D8004 (list 0 entry 0's + 4)

megaman_plain's traces: his buster's flashes (the first kind's type 5, +4 BN5 0x23 and 0x0D, BN6 6 and 5) drawn from list 3's entries 3 and 6 in both, the Cannon's (+4 0x... ) from entry 1; the sparks (the fourth kind's type 4) of a shot from list 5's 5 and of the Cannon from list 5's 1 in both; the charge glow (type 8) from list 5's 8 in both

power_attack.why: MegaMan's AI data +4 to +8 and +0x11 name his power attacks (his charged shot's at +7, BPwrAtk), each an entry of each game's table (BN5 0x0800F368, 108 entries; Gregar 0x080117D4, 148, grown by the Souls track's S4 to 159 in the Souls' room, soul_room.h's SOULS_POWERS, the word 0x080117D0 pointed at the copy): BN5's number read as BN6's. In both games his plain loadout is ff ff 00 01 ff ff (no Cross, no Soul: the normal charged shot, entry 1 of each, BN5 0x0800F5B4 and Gregar 0x08011A7E, 10 x (Attack + 1)), and 0xFF none: the same numbers. A Soul's are BN6's from SOUL_POWER_FIRST (0x94) in the recipe's order (tools/xsoul.py's POWERS: ColonelSoul's charged shot 0x14 and chip shot 0x13, ShadowSoul's charged shot 0x17 and B+Left 0x45, NumberSoul's 0x07, TomahawkSoul's 0x1A, KnightSoul's 0x11, ToadSoul's 0x2D), then the three whose BN5 routine is the empty one, their charge times alone read (the A button's chip charge: 0x12, 0x18, 0x1B); a Chaos Unison's attack (+0x11) none yet (the Souls track's S6).
evidence: src/emu/soulpower.c's tables(): the grown table, BN5's rows of 0x0801CA18 by the Soul written in BN6's ids into SOULS_LOADOUTS, the loadout's read (0x0800FEEC) hooked to them for the proxy form with a Soul; soulcode_bn5.c's powers

flash.why: An arm's flash (the first kind's type 5, the image object) names its kind at +4, an entry of each game's table of kinds (BN5 0x080B9A5C, BN6 0x080BA444, 5 bytes each: its sprite's list and number, animation, height and arm flag), which the two lay out otherwise. The Souls' code and MegaMan's buster in a Soul spawn BN5's own object, moved (issue #82's allocations, their amendment: one BN5 object for every track, its kinds table BN5's; tools/bn5_twins.py's MOVE_TYPES): through BN5's spawner moved with the Souls' code (tools/xsoul.py), BN6's buster's call of its spawner sent there in a Soul (src/emu/soullook.c), its type the second-level dispatch's (read as 5, legit.json's types), its kinds BN5's numbers, their sprites given BN6's numbers. So a flash's kind is the same number in both: no map. Any other flash compared as it is (MegaMan's own buster's: the mask 'MegaMan's buster flash').
evidence: soulcode_bn5.c's types (1, 0x05 moved, BN5 0x080B9B81) and bytes (the kinds 0x03, 0x0A, 0x23, 0x31, 0x32 and 0x33 their sprites as BN6 lists them); soul_colonel's t203: ColonelSoul's flash kind 3 in both

souls.why: A Soul's state: BN5 keeps it in MegaMan's AI data (its turns +0x0F, its chaos +0x12, the chaos charge's phase +0x1F, ColonelSoul's chip +0x32, 0xFFFF none, the chaos level +0x6C) and names the Soul by his form byte; BN6's engine keeps it in the Souls' block (BN6_SOULS, a side's 0x20 bytes: +0 the Soul, +1 chaos, +2 turns, +3 phase, +4 the chip, 0 none, +6 level, +0x10 the Souls used this battle), as BN6's AI data has its own fields at those places (+0x0F a turn guard, +0x12 the HP bug's level, +0x32 tired). So BN5's AI data reads 0 at those places (its Soul's state compared here instead), its used word (BN5_SOULS_USED) against the block's, and BN6's Crosses' used word must be 0 (BN5 has no Cross). The block's other bytes are BN6's engine's own bookkeeping (+7 the opening's mood set, +8-+0xA the Soul committed and not yet entered, +0xB element 0xB's role, +0xC what stands under OK): not compared. Element 0xB (UNITE, BN5_CUSTOM_UNITE and BN6_CUSTOM_UNITE) is compared byte for byte as each game's last Custom screen left it.
evidence: BN5: AIData +0x0F set to the record's turns as he unites (0x080120FC) and counted down as each Custom screen opens (0x080124A2); +0x12 1 for Chaos Unison (0x08012164); +0x32 the record's +6 (0x080124A6, from the sequencer 0x08011DD4); the used word 0x02034E10 ORed at OK (0x08025042)

BN6: BN6_SOULS written by src/emu/soullife.c (entering and leaving form 8, the countdown at 0x08008472/0x0800847C) and soulunite.c (OK's commit: the used bit); BN6's own AIData +0x0F (0x08015A16, 0x080159C6), +0x12 (0x0801026A), +0x32 (0x0801443C)

collision.why: A collision data is 0xA0 bytes in BN5 and 0xA8 in BN6, laid out otherwise from +0x14: each segment is (BN5's offset, BN6's, bytes), found by pairing the two games' routines (the symbol map's pairs whose instructions agree but for an offset on a register loaded from an object's +0x54) and checked against both traces. Where one game keeps in two bytes or words what the other keeps in one, BN5's parts are checked by their rule (bn5_or: the word BN5 ORs them into, which is compared with BN6's); a byte of either outside the segments and the rules must be zero in both. The flag words (flag_words, BN6's offsets) hold bits, never addresses, so they are compared as bytes even where they look like a ROM address.
evidence: +0x00-0x13 the same: the paired routines' accesses at +1, +2, +6, +9, +0xA, +0xB, +0xC, +0xD, +0xE, +0xF, +0x10, +0x11 agree (e.g. BN5 0x08016B64 / BN6 0x0801A050, the collision panels' update); the setup BN5 0x08016760 / BN6 0x08019FB4 writes +1, +2, +4, +7, +0xA, +0xE alike

BN5 +0x14 is BN6 +0x64: BN5 0x080C4BC4 / BN6 0x080C6A08, the same attack's routine storing a word from its table; the hit pass adds the hitter's word there into BN5 +0x98 / BN6 +0xA0 (0x08016AE2 / 0x081D7922)

masks.name: the engine's draws while the battle's clock holds
masks.why: Both games draw three random numbers each frame whatever the battle does (rng, per_frame: the game state's GetRNG and GetRNGSecondary, the main loop's GetRNGSecondary), the battle's clock (its timer) still or not. Where it holds for a number of frames each game's own, each game's words step as many times more as it had frames more, and the first traced frame after shows them apart; rng=follow writes BN6's from BN5's after it. Two holds differ: a turn's change opened with L takes BN6 four frames more than BN5 (three as it begins: BN6 runs its turn's form check before its Custom screen, 0x0800840C calling 0x0801483C, which BN5 skips in a battle not linked, 0x0800773C through 0x0802D510; one more as the turn starts after it, 52 frames against 53); and a Soul's unison is BN5's own crossing, longer than the proxy's (the summon behind it HeatMan's, src/emu/soulproxy.c) by 6 frames, until the Souls track's S3 brings BN5's image. The engine's, not the Soul's: held only where every other draw since the last traced frame is the same in number in both and each word is the other's stepped by exactly the per-frame draws one game made more.
evidence: soul_knight, the frames of each hold (src/dev/xdiff.c's trace and the cores' frames): at t523 BN5 2 frames of the fight's phase then 52 of the Custom screen's closed window, BN6 5 and 53 (the Custom screen itself the same, 37 frames); at t0 BN5 194 frames, BN6 188 (the unison against the proxy's crossing)
